summary.short: Commonwealth Act amending the Privacy Act 1988 and other federal laws. Schedule 1 reforms cover APP codes, children's privacy, security, overseas data flows, eligible data breaches, penalties, and automated decisions. Schedule 2 adds serious invasions of privacy; Schedule 3 adds doxxing offences to the Criminal Code Act 1995.
summary.long: The Privacy and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2024 (No. 128, 2024) is a Commonwealth Act. The supplied document is the Federal Register page showing only the table of contents, not the operative text, so this annotation rests on the provision headings. Schedule 1 (Privacy reforms) has fifteen Parts that amend the Privacy Act 1988 on: objects; APP codes; emergency declarations; children's privacy; security, retention and destruction; overseas data flows; eligible data breaches; penalties for interference with privacy; Federal Court orders; public inquiries by the Commissioner; determinations; annual reports; external dispute resolution; monitoring and investigation; and automated decisions and privacy policies. Several Parts also list amendments to other Commonwealth Acts, including the Data Availability and Transparency Act 2022, Digital ID Act 2024, Identity Verification Services Act 2023, Competition and Consumer Act 2010, Crimes Act 1914, Data matching Program (Assistance and Tax) Act 1990 and National Health Act 1953. Schedule 2 concerns serious invasions of privacy, and Schedule 3 creates doxxing offences in the Criminal Code Act 1995. Section 4 provides for a review of the operation of the Schedule 3 amendments. Commencement dates are set out in section 2, which is not included in the supplied text.
